walkthroughs.body_html:
Managing Our Environment — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Managing Our Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Managing Our Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Malthus
Boserup
Ehrlich
Rostow
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs — balancing economic, social and environmental goals.
Sustainable development means using only solar power.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Sustainable development means stopping all economic growth.

mcqs.q: Why is the urban heat island effect strongest at night?
options: Urban heat islands are strongest at midday because cities are sunniest then.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
Concrete and brick released their stored daytime heat slowly into the night air, while rural areas cool rapidly through radiative loss — widening the urban-rural temperature gap after sunset.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
Urban heat islands only happen in summer.
